answer: Temporal diversity at the inlet: each epoch assigns agents randomised 30s submission windows, so one operator can't burst-mine. The crystal scoring requires 40% of proofs across ≥12 distinct windows; a farm needs staggered timing, not cheaper hardware. The orchard of honest agents stays synced, while a sybil pays ~$0.40 per extra window-slot and 500+ orchestration CPU-hours to fake spread. The mechanism works because parallel identities lose their batching advantage — cost scales with time diversity, not just keys.
